paper.title: Regret Analysis of Stochastic and Nonstochastic Multi-armed Bandit Problems

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic bandit with rewards satisfying the psi moment condition
unmapped: rewards satisfy log E exp(lambda(X-EX)) <= psi(lambda) and log E exp(lambda(EX-X)) <= psi(lambda) for a known convex psi (eq. psicond); learner knows psi
settings.definition_quote: There exists a convex function $\psi$ on the reals such that, for all $\lambda \geq 0$, $\ln \E\,e^{\lambda (X-\E[X])} \leq \psi(\lambda)$ and $\ln\,\E\,e^{\lambda (\E[X] - X)} \leq \psi(\lambda)$.
Consider a strategy that satisfies $\E\,T_i(n) = o(n^a)$ for any set of Bernoulli reward distributions
simultaneously, the adversary selects a gain vector $g_t=(g_{1,t},\hdots,g_{K,t}) \in [0,1]^K$, possibly with the help of external randomization
The bound \eqref{eq:exp3boundanytime} is obtained assuming that the forecaster does not know the number of rounds $n$.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial bandit with non-oblivious adversary (high probability / expected regret)
settings.definition_quote: In the general case of a non-oblivious adversary, the loss vector at time $t$ depends on the past actions of the forecaster. ... One way around this difficulty is to first prove high probability bounds, and then integrate the resulting bound.

settings.name_in_paper: Minimax lower bound over i.i.d. Bernoulli rewards
settings.definition_quote: Let $\sup$ be the supremum over all distribution of rewards such that, for $i=1,\dots,K$, the rewards $Y_{i,1},Y_{i,2},\ldots\in\{0,1\}$ are i.i.d., and let $\inf$ be the infimum over all forecasters.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with side information (finite context set, adversarial rewards)
unmapped: finite context set S, sequence of contexts arbitrary but fixed; compete with best mapping from contexts to arms
settings.definition_quote: game rounds $t=1,2,\dots$ are marked by contexts $s_1,s_2,\dots$ from a given context set $\cS$. The forecaster must learn the best mapping $g : \cS \to \{1,\dots,K\}$ ... we further assume that the sequence of contexts $s_t$ is arbitrary but fixed.

unmapped: learner knows number of experts N; expert advice may depend on forecaster's past random plays
settings.definition_quote: at each step $t=1,2,\dots$ the forecaster obtains the expert advice $(\xi_t^1,\dots,\xi_t^N)$, where each $\xi_t^j$ is a probability distribution over arms ... We allow the expert advice to depend on the realization of the forecaster's past random plays.

settings.name_in_paper: Competing against the best context set
unmapped: class of context sets {S_theta}; compete with best theta and best mapping S_theta -> arms
settings.definition_quote: Consider now a class $\theset{\cS_{\theta}}{\theta\in\Theta}$ of context sets. In this new game, each time step $t=1,2,\dots$ is marked by the vector $(s_{\theta,t})_{\theta\in\Theta}$ of contexts

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic contextual bandits with a VC class of policies
unmapped: policy class F of binary policies with VC dimension d given to the learner
settings.definition_quote: contexts $x_t$ and arm losses $\ell_t$ are realizations of i.i.d. draws from a fixed and unknown distribution $D$ over $\cX \times [0,1]^K$ ... we focus on the case of $K=2$ arms and parametrize classes $\cF$ of policies by their VC-dimension $d$

unmapped: feedback is only whether predicted label is correct; comparator is cumulative hinge loss of linear multiclass classifier U
settings.definition_quote: In the bandit version, the learner only observes $\ds1_{\yhat_t \neq y_t}$; that is, whether the prediction at time $t$ was correct or not.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial linear bandit, finite action set, bounded scalar loss
settings.definition_quote: we assume that $\cK$ and $\cL$ are such that $|x^{\top} \ell| \leq 1$ for any $(x, \ell) \in \cK \times \cL$. Moreover, we restrict our attention to finite sets $\cK$, with $|\cK| = N$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online combinatorial optimization with semi-bandit feedback
unmapped: actions C subset {0,1}^d with ||v||_1 = m, losses in [0,1]^d
settings.definition_quote: the set of arms is $\cC \subseteq \{0,1\}^d$ and the set of linear loss functions is $\cL = [0,1]^d$. We assume $\norm{v}_1 = m$ for all $v\in\cC$

settings.name_in_paper: Online linear optimization with bandit feedback on the Euclidean ball
unmapped: loss vectors in the Euclidean unit ball
settings.definition_quote: Let $\cK = \cL = \{x \in \R^d \,:\, \norm{x} \leq 1 \}$ define an online linear optimization problem with bandit feedback.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial bandit convex optimization with two-point feedback
unmapped: r B subset K subset R B with r, R known
settings.definition_quote: Let $\cK\subseteq\R^d$ be a closed convex set such that $r\,\Ball\subseteq\cK\subseteq R\,\Ball$ for some $r,R > 0$. Let $\cL$ be a set of $G$-Lipschitz differentiable and convex losses.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial bandit convex optimization with one-point feedback
unmapped: losses convex and differentiable, uniformly bounded by L (known)
r B subset K subset R B with r, R known
settings.definition_quote: Let $\cL$ be a set of $G$-Lipschitz differentiable and convex losses, uniformly bounded by $L$ (that is $||\ell||_{\infty} \leq L, \forall \ell \in \cL$).

settings.name_in_paper: Nonlinear stochastic bandit on [0,1] with unimodal mean loss
unmapped: growth condition |mu(x)-mu(x')| >= C_L|x-x'| away from the minimizer, C_L known to learner
settings.definition_quote: arms are points in the unit interval $[0,1]$ ... the loss is the realization of an independent random variable $Y_t\in [0,1]$ with expected value $\mu(x_t)$ ... we assume that $\mu : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ is unimodal

algorithms.name: OSMD on the Euclidean ball with F(x)=-ln(1-||x||)-||x||

conditions: reward distributions satisfy the psi moment condition (eq. psicond)

source.label: th:ucb
source.quote: Assume that the reward distributions satisfy \eqref{eq:psicond}. Then $(\alpha, \psi)$-UCB with $\alpha > 2$ satisfies $$\oR_n \leq \sum_{i \,:\, \Delta_i > 0} \left( \frac{\alpha \Delta_i}{\psi^*(\Delta_i / 2)} \ln n + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 2}  \right)~.$$

results.notes: Survey restatement; UCB from Auer et al. 2002. Index uses ln t so no horizon needed.

source.label: eq:regretUCBbounded
source.quote: In case of $[0,1]$-valued random variables, taking $\psi(\lambda) = \tfrac{\lambda^2}{8}$ ... gives $\psi^*(\epsilon) = 2 \epsilon^2$, which in turns gives the following pseudo-regret bound $\oR_n \leq \sum_{i : \Delta_i > 0} \left( \frac{2 \alpha}{\Delta_i} \ln n + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 2}  \right)$

results.notes: Special case of Theorem th:ucb (alpha-UCB) for bounded rewards; recorded separately since expression differs.

conditions: strategy satisfies E T_i(n) = o(n^a) for all Bernoulli instances, all suboptimal i, all a>0

source.label: th:LR85
source.quote: Consider a strategy that satisfies $\E\,T_i(n) = o(n^a)$ for any set of Bernoulli reward distributions, any arm $i$ with $\Delta_i > 0$, and any $a>0$. Then, for any set of Bernoulli reward distributions the following holds $$\liminf_{n \to +\infty} \frac{\oR_n}{\ln n} \geq \sum_{i \,:\, \Delta_i > 0} \frac{\Delta_i}{\kl(\mu_i,\mu^*)}~.$$

results.notes: Extracted from Lai & Robbins (1985), restricted to Bernoulli. Proof given only for two arms.

source.label: th:Exp3
source.quote: If Exp3 is run with $\eta_t=\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2 \ln K}{n K}}$, then \oR_n \leq \sqrt{2 n K \ln K}~.

results.notes: Exp3 from Auer et al. 2002; proof from Bubeck 2010. Adversary type not specified for pseudo-regret.

source.label: th:Exp3
source.quote: Moeover, if Exp3 is run with $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K}{t K}}$, then \oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{n K \ln K}~.

results.notes: Anytime version.

source.label: th:exp3P
source.quote: For any given $\delta \in (0,1)$, if Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln(K \delta^{-1})}{n K}}, \eta = 0.95 \sqrt{\frac{\ln(K)}{n K}}, \gamma = 1.05 \sqrt{\frac{K \ln(K)}{n}}$ then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, R_n \leq 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln(K \delta^{-1})}~.

results.notes: Holds against any (incl. non-oblivious) adversary.

source.label: th:exp3P
source.quote: Moreover, if Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\tfrac{\ln(K)}{n K}}$ while $\eta$ and $\gamma$ are chosen as before, then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, R_n \leq \sqrt{\frac{n K}{\ln(K)}} \ln(\delta^{-1}) + 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln(K)}~.

results.notes: Holds simultaneously for all delta (delta not an input).

source.quote: If Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K }{n K}}, \eta = 0.95 \sqrt{\frac{\ln K }{n K}}, \gamma = 1.05 \sqrt{\frac{K \ln K }{n}}$ then \E\,R_n \leq 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln K} + \sqrt{\frac{n K}{\ln K }}~.

results.notes: Unlabelled theorem; obtained by integrating the high-probability bound.

source.label: th:LBminimax
source.quote: Let $\sup$ be the supremum over all distribution of rewards such that, for $i=1,\dots,K$, the rewards $Y_{i,1},Y_{i,2},\ldots\in\{0,1\}$ are i.i.d., and let $\inf$ be the infimum over all forecasters. Then \inf \sup (...) \geq \frac{1}{20} \sqrt{n K}

results.notes: From Auer et al. 2002. Implies lower bound on adversarial expected regret too.

tuning: one instance of Exp3 per context

source.label: th:context-simple
source.quote: There exists a randomized forecaster for bandits with side information (the $\cS$-Exp3 forecaster, defined in the proof) that satisfies \oRS_n \le \sqrt{2n |\cS| K\ln K} for any set $\cS$ of contexts.

results.notes: Proof applies the known-horizon Exp3 bound per context with n_s rounds, implicitly tuning each instance with n_s. Due to Maillard & Munos 2011.

source.label: th:Exp4
source.quote: Exp4 without mixing and with $\eta_t=\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2 \ln N}{n K}}$ satisfies \oRx_n \leq \sqrt{2 n N \ln K}~.

results.notes: Recorded as printed. This is almost certainly a typo: the proof gives log N/eta + (K/2) sum eta_t, i.e. sqrt(2 n K ln N), consistent with the text's 'bound of order sqrt(nK ln N)'.

source.label: th:Exp4
source.quote: On the other hand, with $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln N}{t K}}$ it satisfies \oRx_n \leq 2 \sqrt{n N \ln K}~.

results.notes: Recorded as printed; likely typo for 2 sqrt(n K ln N) per the proof. Anytime tuning.

symbols.eps_q: lower bound on every probability of the sampling distributions q_t actually used to draw arms

conditions: arms are drawn from arbitrary history-dependent distributions q_t with q_{t,i} >= eps_q > 0

source.label: th:exp3-rebel
source.quote: Consider a $K$-armed bandit game in which at each step the played arm $I_t$ is drawn from an arbitrary distribution $q_t$ ... $q_{t,i} \ge \ve > 0$ ... If Exp3 without mixing is run with $\tilde{\ell}_{i,t} = \frac{\ell_{i,t}}{q_{i,t}} \ds1_{I_t = i}$ and $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2\ln K}{n K}}$ then max_k E[sum E_{i~p_t} l_{i,t} - sum l_{k,t}] \le \sqrt{\frac{2 n}{\ve}\ln K}

results.notes: Regret is of Exp3's own distribution p_t while plays come from q_t; quantity 'other'. Intermediate tool for the context-set result.

source.label: th:exp4-mixing
source.quote: Exp4 with mixing coefficient $\gamma$ and with $\eta_t = \eta = \gamma/K$ satisfies \oRx_n \le \frac{\gamma\,n}{2} + \frac{K\ln N}{\gamma}~.

results.notes: Bound for free gamma; horizon dependence only through tuning choice of gamma.

symbols.S_max: max over theta of |S_theta|, size of largest context set

tuning: gamma of order n^{-1/3}(max|S_theta| K ln K)^{1/3} sqrt(ln|Theta|)

source.label: th:theta-regret
source.quote: There exists a randomized forecaster achieving \oR^{\Theta}_n = \mathcal{O}\left(n^{2/3}\left(\max_{\theta\in\Theta}|\cS_{\theta}|K\ln K\right)^{1/3}\sqrt{\ln|\Theta|}\right) for any class of context sets.

results.notes: Exp4 with mixing using S-Exp3 instances as experts; due to Maillard & Munos 2011.

symbols.d_VC: VC dimension of the policy class

conditions: K = 2 arms, binary policy class of VC dimension d

source.label: eq:vebound
source.quote: For any class $\cF$ of binary policies of VC-dimension $d$ and for all $n > d$, the forecaster VE run with $n' = \sqrt{n\left(2d\ln\frac{en}{d}+ \ln\frac{3}{\delta}\right)}$ satisfies ... \leq c\sqrt{n\left(d\ln\frac{en}{d} + \ln\frac{3}{\delta}\right)} for some constant $c > 0$ and with probability at least $1-\delta$

results.notes: Regret is realized loss vs n times the risk of the best policy. From Beygelzimer et al. 2011. VE simulates Exp4.P over a possibly exponentially large class; compute not stated.

conditions: |x^T l| <= 1 for all actions and losses
action set finite with N = K elements spanning R^d

source.label: th:exp2john
source.quote: For any $\eta,\gamma > 0$ such that ${\eta d} \le {\gamma}$, Exp2 with John's exploration satisfies $\oR_n \leq 2 \gamma n + \frac{\ln N}{\eta} + \eta n d$. In particular, with $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln N}{3 n d}}$ and $\gamma = \eta d$, $\oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{3 n d \ln N}~.$

results.notes: Paper's N = |K| mapped to canonical K (number of actions). General bound 2γn + ln N/η + ηnd also stated. From Bubeck, Cesa-Bianchi, Kakade 2012.

source.label: th:osmdnegent
source.quote: For any set $\cC\subseteq\{0,1\}^d$, if OSMD is run on $\cK=\conv(\cC)$ with $F(x) = \sum_{i=1}^d x_i \ln x_i - \sum_{i=1}^d x_i$ ... In particular, with the estimate \eqref{eq:semibanditestimate} and $\eta= \sqrt{\frac{2m}{nd}\ln\frac{d}{m}}$, $\oR_n \leq  \sqrt{2 m d n \ln \frac{d}{m}}~.$

results.notes: From Audibert, Bubeck, Lugosi 2011. Projection step may be computationally hard for some C.

symbols.q_pot: exponent q > 1 of the potential psi(x) = (-x)^{-q}

source.label: th:osmdzero
source.quote: In particular, choosing the $0$-potential $\psi(x) = (- x)^{-q}$, the estimate~\eqref{eq:semibanditestimate}, and $\eta= \sqrt{\frac{2}{q-1} \frac{m^{1 - 2/q}}{d^{1 - 2/q}}}$, $\oR_n \leq q \sqrt{\frac{2}{q-1} m d n}~.$

results.notes: As printed, eta has no n-dependence (likely missing 1/sqrt(n)); recorded the stated bound. For m=1 this is INF for the adversarial MAB.

source.label: th:osmdzero
source.quote: With $q=2$ this gives $$\oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{2 m d n}~.$$

results.notes: q=2 case of r20; with m=1 gives log-free sqrt(nK) bound for adversarial MAB.

source.quote: Fix $\delta > 0$ and assume OSGD is run on $(1-\tfrac{\delta}{r})\cK$ with learning rate $\eta > 0$ and gradient estimates ... Then the following holds \oR_n \le \frac{R^2}{\eta} + \eta (Gd)^2 n + \delta\left(3 + \frac{R}{r} \right) G n~.

_verify.summary: I found no errors to correct in this extraction. Every expression, constant and tuning I checked matches the paper's statements, and the extractor recorded the misprinted Exp4 bounds exactly as printed while noting the typo. The paper is a survey, so all results are correctly marked is_new=false. One judgement call: they stay in results rather than cited_results because the survey gives its own proofs. The general free-parameter forms of a few theorems (for example Exp2, the OSMD negative-entropy bound and the Euclidean-ball bound) were not recorded separately. That is a small gap in coverage, not an error.
